oracle.why: This is the direct parser used by the most-downloaded current npm Obsidian-flavored Markdown integration. npm's official point API reported 43,766 direct-package downloads for 2026-08-23..2026-08-29; the 44,174-download umbrella package delegates parsing to it.

candidateDownloads.note: umbrella transformer; delegates parsing to the selected package

metadataOracle.runner: gray-matter custom yaml engine / js-yaml JSON_SCHEMA
metadataOracle.why: No executable Obsidian parser API is available. gray-matter is the most-downloaded current dedicated frontmatter parser among the compared packages, and js-yaml is its ecosystem's dominant maintained YAML decoder. npm's official point API reported 8,940,668 and 298,229,346 downloads respectively for the recorded week.

candidateDownloads.note: syntax tokenizer only; does not decode values

metadataOracle.authorityBoundary: The official Properties page owns exact placement and fence grammar. The packages supply executable evidence only for successful forms in their documented intersection; permissive package-only syntax is not accepted by the target contract.

claim: For the documented constructs the selected package actually parses, Markdown Core must converge on the same semantic recognition except for explicit, general AST-model deltas. The official Obsidian documentation, not this package, owns the language contract.

baselineGaps.requirement: Recognize a wikilink and expose Destination.cross(path, anchor=null) instead of one literal Text node.
Preserve the vault path and complete anchor value in one Destination.cross value, plus the CrossLink label.
Recognize the shared wikilink form with embedded=true and preserve its label/size parameter.
Recognize an embedded block reference and project it to the same Destination.cross.anchor field as a heading reference, without the #^ delimiter or a source-kind tag.
Recognize highlighted content instead of retaining the delimiter bytes as text.
Recognize and, under the Obsidian preset, omit an inline comment without consuming surrounding text.
Treat a multiline comment as opaque and omit the whole construct under the Obsidian preset.
Recognize a non-space task character as complete and remove the marker from visible item content.

modelDeltas.summary: The oracle emits the complete highlight body as one Text child. The target Markdown Core AST parses it as inline content, like emphasis and strikethrough.
modelDeltas.handling: The comparison keeps children today so the basic plain-text witness agrees after recognition. Nested-format product fixtures are not projected through this oracle.

modelDeltas.summary: mdast uses half-open unist points with JavaScript string offsets while Markdown Core publishes inherited inclusive line/column scopes.
modelDeltas.handling: The comparison omits scopes on both sides. Product correctness and shared canonical fixtures own positions.

modelDeltas.summary: The oracle collapses an absent wikilink label delimiter to an empty alias string, while the target model distinguishes an absent label from an authored empty label.
modelDeltas.handling: The projection consults the node's exact source spelling and maps the oracle's empty alias to null only when no label delimiter was authored.

modelDeltas.summary: mdast stores ordinary link/image URLs and wikilink path/heading components as flat fields. The target model stores one tagged Destination value.
modelDeltas.handling: The semantic projection wraps ordinary link/image URLs in Destination.url and wikilinks in Destination.cross; both heading and block spellings populate the same optional anchor after source punctuation is removed.

modelDeltas.summary: mdast stores an image's alt text as one string, while the target Image owns parsed inline content.
modelDeltas.handling: The semantic projection maps a non-empty mdast alt string to one Text child. The corpus exercises the plain-text intersection; product fixtures own nested inline image-alt structure.

modelDeltas.summary: mdast names every inherited > container blockquote, while the target canonical AST uses Callout for both metadata-free and metadata-bearing quoted containers.
modelDeltas.handling: The semantic projection maps mdast blockquote to Callout. The inherited source grammar remains owned by CommonMark; official product fixtures own optional Obsidian metadata.

modelDeltas.summary: js-yaml exposes finite numbers as JavaScript Number values, while the target Metadata model retains the exact authored numeric spelling to avoid cross-platform precision loss.
modelDeltas.handling: The oracle corpus uses exactly representable canonical spellings and projects them with String(value). Product fixtures own large integers, exponents, negative zero, and other cases where numeric spelling or precision is observable.

modelDeltas.summary: gray-matter and js-yaml expose decoded data and body content but do not publish the source-faithful Metadata and MetadataRecord scopes required by the target AST.
modelDeltas.handling: The parity comparison omits scopes. Product fixtures own exact fence, record, continuation-line, alias-occurrence, body, and Document ranges.

modelDeltas.summary: js-yaml returns a JavaScript object, whose standard enumeration order moves integer-index-looking property names ahead of other names even when the YAML source authored another order.
modelDeltas.handling: The oracle corpus covers source order with ordinary names. Product fixtures own exact order for numeric-looking and every other valid name; the target AST always follows source order.

modelDeltas.summary: js-yaml exposes mapping keys only after conversion to JavaScript property strings, so it cannot preserve whether a decoded name came from a plain or quoted scalar or reject a sequence, mapping, or alias key by inspecting the resulting object.
modelDeltas.handling: The oracle corpus covers decoded names in the direct-scalar intersection. Product fixtures own property-name source validation, quote-independent decoding, and duplicate detection in the decoded string namespace.

notAnAuthorityFor: CommonMark or GFM syntax; the existing cmark and cmark-gfm policies remain primary.
Obsidian dialect changes to inherited CommonMark behavior, including suppression between paired inline HTML tags. The profile deliberately excludes them.
Tags. The package implements them, but the official OFM extension table does not include them; the gate disables them.
Math delimiter edge cases. The gate disables the package's micromark math extension; documented $ and $$ forms remain under the product formula contract.
Callouts. They are implemented by the umbrella transform after parsing, not by this direct parser package.

Block identifier attachment, inline-footnote recognition, the Cite/Citation/CitationReferent/Footnote consumer projection, or image-size semantics. The selected Markdown comparison does not implement them, so official-example product fixtures own them.

Properties syntax accepted only by gray-matter, YAML values outside the documented Obsidian domain, property-name source shapes erased by js-yaml, strict invalid-candidate fallback, exact numeric spellings, source scopes, or resource limits. Product fixtures own these boundaries.
Vault resolution, rendering, styling, editor completion, or transclusion. These are outside a parser-only AST.
